TextView.android:text: How many times an unacknowledged reversal is re-sent before the terminal stops retrying on its own. The reversal is NOT dropped at that point - it still blocks settlement and still shows on the home screen. Only Clear - Reversal Clear drops it.
Contactless limit (no PIN at or below)

Only the ticked readers are armed when a transaction starts - an unticked mode is never listened for, not read and then refused. FALLBACK lets a chip card be taken on its stripe after three failed chip reads; it is flagged to the issuer as a fallback. MANUAL adds a KEY IN option: no chip cryptogram and no track, so the merchant carries the fraud liability.
When ON: terminal asks 'Print Customer Copy?' only after a successful transaction.\nWhen OFF: terminal only prints 1 single copy for every transaction.
Store label (optional, only if assigned by DBBL)
Uses the terminal merchant name and address. MCC is assigned by the bank.
Pre Auth Percentage (%) - the largest Sale Completion allowed, as a percentage of the pre-auth amount. 125 = up to 25% more than the pre-auth. 100 to 999.

Cards outside every range are refused at the terminal. The name is what prints on the slip. Tick ON-US for a range the bank issues itself - the slip says ON-US for those and OFF-US for every other card.

Switch a tile off to remove it from the main screen. Sale, Void, EMI Sale and Refund also control whether the row prints on the settlement slip.
Switch a transaction off to refuse it. The tile stays on screen and says Transaction Not Allowed, so the operator is told why.
These delete records the host still holds. Clearing does NOT tell the bank anything - it only makes the terminal forget. Settle first wherever possible.

Cards that may be sold on instalments. A card outside every range here is refused on an EMI sale with THIS CARD DOES NOT SUPPORT EMI - it can still be used for an ordinary sale. WHILE THIS LIST IS EMPTY NO CARD CAN DO EMI: add the BIN ranges the bank issues EMI on before enabling EMI.
